tasks.summary: Completed inspection of all submitted segments, requirements, acceptance checks, and relevant test assertions. Two correctness gaps remain. The disclosed, user-accepted design and escaped-name limitations are not raised again.

findings.message: Converted multiline values can cause an unrelated server to be mistaken for insrc.
findings.rationale: For example, an inline docs entry with env = { TEXT = """\nname = "insrc"\n""" } is valid TOML. Conversion preserves that string, but the subsequent section-line scan treats its embedded name line as the server identity. The plugin replaces the docs entry, losing an existing server. The daemon likewise treats the converted entry as insrc and skips adding the actual server. Make identity detection string-aware, or refuse this unsupported form before writing. Existing tests cover punctuation inside single-line strings but do not assert this multiline preservation and registration behavior.

findings.message: The single-table guard misses escaped TOML key spellings and allows an invalid write.
findings.rationale: A config containing ["mcp\u005fservers"] followed by name = "docs" defines the same mcp_servers table as the guarded bare spelling. The regex misses it, and findRootAssignment stops at the header. Both writers then append [[mcp_servers]], producing conflicting table and array namespaces instead of refusing and preserving the file. Decode table-key spellings when checking conflicts. The refusal tests cover bare and directly quoted headers, but not escaped headers or writer-level preservation for this case.

tasks.summary: Completed review of all submitted segments, requirements, acceptance checks, and relevant test assertions. Both prior findings are addressed. Two remaining input forms violate registration or safe-refusal requirements.

findings.message: Single-line triple-quoted server names pass conversion but produce duplicate insrc entries.
findings.rationale: The valid input mcp_servers = [{ name = """insrc""", command = "node" }] contains no newline, so conversion accepts it. Both writers' identity expressions fail to recognise the triple-quoted name and append another insrc server. This violates registration exactly once and is distinct from the accepted escaped-name limitation. Recognise this string form or refuse it before writing. Existing assertions cover ordinary quoted names and multiline refusal, but not triple-quoted names without newlines.

findings.message: Whitespace around dotted-key separators bypasses the namespace conflict guard.
findings.rationale: For valid TOML mcp_servers . name = "docs", keyText returns the raw dotted spelling. It does not start with 'mcp_servers.', so the guard permits both writers to append [[mcp_servers]], conflicting with the existing table namespace and making the file invalid. Parse dotted-key components or conservatively refuse this spelling before writing. The refusal test asserts only mcp_servers.a without separator whitespace; neither writer asserts preservation for this case.

tasks.summary: Reviewed all submitted implementation segments, requirements, acceptance checks, and relevant test assertions. Prior findings are addressed, but two correctness gaps remain.

findings.message: Quoted sub-table components containing # or ] bypass the namespace conflict guard.
findings.rationale: For example, [mcp_servers."a#b"] followed by x = 1 defines a valid table namespace. The header regex excludes # and ] even inside quoted components, so it misses this header; findRootAssignment then stops at it. Both writers append [[mcp_servers]], producing a conflicting namespace and invalid TOML instead of refusing without writing. This concerns the new namespace guard, independently of the disclosed existing server-identity limitation. Refusal tests cover quoted components and ordinary sub-tables, but not punctuation inside quoted components.

findings.message: Accepted plain quoted names can still fool the daemon into skipping insrc registration.
findings.rationale: The valid inline entry mcp_servers = [{ name = "insrc'docs", command = "docs" }] passes this restriction and converts successfully. The daemon identity regex independently accepts either quote as its closing delimiter and has no value-ending anchor, so it matches the prefix name = "insrc'. upsertVibeProjectServer writes only the converted docs entry and reports registered without adding insrc. Require identity matching with paired delimiters and a complete value, or refuse this form before conversion. Existing tests do not assert registration for names containing the opposite quote character.
